congruity

/kon-GROO-ih-tee/ - the stress falls on GROO · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Congruity means agreement or harmony between things.

Reviewers noted the congruity between the cookbook's rustic recipes and its rough linen cover - the object felt like the food.

Example

The landscape architect chose river stones from the same valley, cedar from the same slope, and paths that followed the old sheep tracks, so visitors kept remarking on the garden's congruity with the hills around it: nothing in it argued with its setting.

Congruity is more exact than resemblance because it does not mean two things look alike - it means they fit together, agree, and sit in harmony. The stones do not resemble the cedar; they simply belong together.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

harmony: Harmony is the pleasing effect when combined elements - voices, colors, moods - sound or feel good together. Congruity is quieter and more structural: it says the parts genuinely fit and agree, whether or not the result is beautiful. A report can find congruity between figures no one would call lovely.

agreement: Agreement means two positions, accounts, or parties line up - witnesses agree, or the totals in two ledgers do. Congruity is broader than stated positions: it is the fit between things of any kind - a soundtrack and a film, a frame and a painting.

consistency: Consistency is holding to the same standard or pattern over time - the same recipe followed exactly, batch after batch. Congruity is agreement between different things, not faithfulness to one's own past: parts fitting one another as a whole. A baker shows consistency; a menu and a dining room show congruity.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

mismatch: a pairing that fails to fit

clash: an open conflict between elements

Where it sits · how completely the things match — resemblance → congruity → identity

resemblance vs. congruity: Resemblance only means two things look somewhat alike; congruity is stronger - the parts genuinely agree and fit together as a whole.

identity vs. congruity: Identity goes beyond congruity: congruous things fit together while remaining different things, but identity means no difference is left at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — congru-

Root — congru-: to come together, agree (Latin congruere)

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state of being

Put it together

Put it together: Congru- (Latin congruere, 'to come together, to agree') + -ity (the state of being) = the state of coming together. English still keeps the adjective congruous, 'fitting, harmonious,' so congruity is the state of being congruous - and the same root gives geometry its word for shapes that match point for point.

Use the root in a new word: incongruous

Use the root in a new word: incongruous: One guest arrived at the beach bonfire in a tuxedo that could not have been more incongruous.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / academic

Congruity belongs to reviews, reports, and analysis - writing that weighs how well parts fit a whole. In everyday speech, say things match or go together; write congruity when the fit itself is your point. Its cousin congruent, which you will meet later in this course and in geometry class, describes shapes that match exactly.
